work.title: Publish and fetch Initiative refs alongside Work manifests
work.description: Add refs/codepatrol/initiative/ to every place the refs projection already names refs/codepatrol/manifest/: the local enumeration, the remote query, the validation of what the remote returned, and the scope filter that narrows a single-Work sync. An Initiative is not owned by one Work, so a scoped sync publishes the Initiative its Work belongs to rather than every Initiative in the repository. Cleanup keeps the rule terminalization already follows — an Initiative ref is never deleted by synchronization, because it is the record of intent behind Works that may themselves be archived. The end state is the one the manifests already have: what the local repository decided, the remote carries, and a fresh clone can read.
acceptance: Synchronizing publishes every Initiative ref the local repository holds, and a fresh clone reads back the same Initiative documents that were written
A sync scoped to one Work publishes that Work's Initiative and no other
Fetching brings down Initiative refs that exist only on the remote, so a second clone mints the next free number rather than one already taken
Synchronization never deletes an Initiative ref, including after every Work of that Initiative is terminal
With no remote, or with the refs projection disabled, publication reports skipped and the local Initiative refs are untouched
The projection end-to-end scenario asserts the Initiative ref exists remotely rather than only that its Works do

result.summary: Initiative refs join the refs projection inside LocalGitRemote.sync only: refs/codepatrol/initiative/ is added to the local for-each-ref enumeration, the ls-remote query and its validation, and the scope filter (via initiativeOfWork, so a scoped sync carries exactly the Work's own Initiative). result.handoff:
# Plan: Publish and fetch Initiative refs alongside Work manifests (INIT-2.1)

## Finding (P1)
The refs projection names refs/codepatrol/manifest/ in exactly four places, all in src/adapters/local-git-remote.ts:
1. matchesScope (line 69) — narrows a single-Work sync.
2. localRefs (line 79) — local enumeration via for-each-ref.
3. remoteRefs (line 87) — the remote query via ls-remote patterns.
4. remoteRefs validation (line 91) — refuses refs outside the known prefixes.

Everything else already works: Initiative refs are minted once by GitManifestStore (initiativeRef at manifest-store.ts:319, enumerated at line 407), PublicationService calls remote.sync only when projections.refs is enabled (publication.ts:144, 284) and reports skipped through the existing unpublishedRefs/undefined paths, and the cleanup loop keys terminal handling off activeWorkId, which only matches refs/heads/codepatrol/work/<id>.

## Product files Build touches
1. src/adapters/local-git-remote.ts — the only production-code change.
2. src/test/local-git-remote.test.ts — real-git round-trip tests.
3. src/test/publication.test.ts — skipped-path assertions.
4. scripts/projection-e2e.mjs — remote Initiative ref assertion.
5. src/test/documentation.test.ts — register the new E2E assertion string.

## Adapter changes (src/adapters/local-git-remote.ts)
- Import initiativeOfWork from ../core/initiative.js.
- localRefs: add "refs/codepatrol/initiative/" to the for-each-ref pattern arguments (line 79).
- remoteRefs: add "refs/codepatrol/initiative/*" to the ls-remote patterns (line 87), and extend the validation condition (line 91) to also accept refs starting with refs/codepatrol/initiative/.
- matchesScope: for a scoped sync, also match ref.startsWith(`refs/codepatrol/initiative/${initiativeOfWork(workId)}-`). The trailing dash matters: it keeps INIT-2- from matching INIT-20-. An Initiative is not owned by one Work, so scope includes exactly the one Initiative the selected Work belongs to — never every Initiative (acceptance 2).
- Nothing else changes. Deliberately untouched:
  - Deletion: deletions and localDeletions are fed only through terminalActiveRefs, which requires activeWorkId(ref) — an Initiative ref never matches, so it is never deleted locally or remotely, including after every Work of that Initiative is terminal (acceptance 4). This is structural; the new tests pin it.
  - publishableOutgoing: workIdForRef returns undefined for Initiative refs, so they are always publishable and never suppressed by incompleteTerminalWorks.
  - Divergence: an Initiative ref whose local and remote hashes differ falls into the existing SYNC_CONFLICT branch, same as manifest refs — correct, since Initiative documents are minted once and immutable.

## Tests
src/test/local-git-remote.test.ts (real git, createBareRemote, following the existing tests' shape):
1. publishes every local Initiative ref and a fresh clone reads back the same documents: source app creates a Work (minting refs/codepatrol/initiative/INIT-0-<slug>), syncs; assert the bare remote carries the Initiative ref with the same hash; a fresh target syncs and GitManifestStore.listInitiatives() on the target returns the identical Initiative document (acceptance 1).
2. a second clone mints the next free number: on that target, apply a new Initiative document through the spec flow and assert the minted id is INIT-1, not INIT-0 (acceptance 3).
3. a scoped sync publishes only the selected Work's Initiative: two Initiatives with one Work each; sync with scope { workId } for the INIT-1 Work; the remote gains refs/codepatrol/initiative/INIT-1-* and not refs/codepatrol/initiative/INIT-0-* (acceptance 2).
4. never deletes an Initiative ref: run a Work to terminal, sync with cleanup (policy helper like the existing tests), assert the terminal work branch is gone remotely while the Initiative ref survives both locally and remotely; repeat the sync and assert it is still there (acceptance 4).

src/test/publication.test.ts:
5. Extend the no-remote lifecycle test (or add a sibling): with no remote, publication.automatic returns undefined and the local refs/codepatrol/initiative/ ref still exists with its original hash.
6. Add a refs-projection-disabled case (projections { refs: false, issue: false, milestone: false, project: false } on an app with remoteRepository): publication reports the sync skipped (git refs empty via unpublishedRefs) and the local Initiative ref is untouched (acceptance 5).

scripts/projection-e2e.mjs + src/test/documentation.test.ts:
7. Next to the existing archive-ref assertion (projection-e2e.mjs:222), add: git ls-remote origin `refs/codepatrol/initiative/${applied.initiative}-*` is non-empty, checked as "the Initiative ref exists remotely" (acceptance 6). Add that exact string to the required-assertions list in documentation.test.ts:117 so the guard test enforces it.

## Acceptance coverage
1. Publish all + fresh-clone read-back — adapter patterns + test 1.
2. Scoped sync publishes that Work's Initiative only — matchesScope via initiativeOfWork + test 3.
3. Fetch brings remote-only Initiative refs down; second clone mints next free number — existing incoming/pulled path + tests 1–2.
4. Never deleted — structural (no code path reaches it) + test 4.
5. No remote / refs projection disabled → skipped, local refs untouched — existing publication paths + tests 5–6.
6. E2E asserts the Initiative ref exists remotely — projection-e2e.mjs + documentation.test.ts guard.

## Verification for Build
npm run verify (typecheck, unit tests, smoke, --help). The projection E2E itself runs in CI against GitHub; locally the documentation.test.ts guard proves the scenario asserts it.

## Non-goals
No changes to PublicationService, projections configuration, manifest-store, or the GitHub projections (Issues/Milestones already project Initiatives). No new commands. No deletion or pruning of Initiative refs under any circumstance.

traces.message: The refs projection names refs/codepatrol/manifest/ in exactly four places, all in src/adapters/local-git-remote.ts: matchesScope (scope filter, line 69), localRefs (for-each-ref enumeration, line 79), remoteRefs (ls-remote query line 87 and returned-ref validation line 91). Initiative refs are minted once by GitManifestStore (initiativeRef, manifest-store.ts:319) and enumerated locally at manifest-store.ts:407; publication.service only calls remote.sync when projections.refs is enabled, so the skipped path needs no change.

Initiative refs join the sync by adding refs/codepatrol/initiative/ to the same four spots: the for-each-ref pattern list, the ls-remote pattern list, the returned-ref validation, and matchesScope. A scoped sync matches refs/codepatrol/initiative/<initiativeId>- derived from the Work id via initiativeOfWork (core/initiative.ts), so one Work publishes its own Initiative and no other; the trailing dash makes INIT-2- never match INIT-20-. No deletion logic changes: activeWorkId only matches work branches, so an Initiative ref can never enter terminalActiveRefs and is structurally never deleted; tests pin that rule.

Tests land in three places: real-git round-trip tests in local-git-remote.test.ts (publish all, scoped publishes only the selected Work's Initiative, fetch lets a fresh clone mint the next free Initiative number, terminal cleanup never deletes the Initiative ref), skipped-path assertions in publication.test.ts (no remote and refs projection disabled leave local Initiative refs untouched), and the projection E2E (scripts/projection-e2e.mjs) gains an ls-remote check that the Initiative ref exists remotely, with the assertion string registered in documentation.test.ts.
